subject: Third-party integration deprecation: mitigation cadence & comms owners
messages:
From: Maya R. <maya@databridge.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Heads up: Acme using legacy /v1/embed endpoint (needs migration)

Hi Karthik,

Quick heads up from our integration team — Acme just confirmed they still have a significant portion of traffic hitting the legacy /v1/embed endpoint and a couple of internal microservices pinned to older model hashes. We did a sweep and attached a short matrix (acme-dep-matrix-v1.xlsx) showing which teams and tokens are on the old path.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm the final cutover windows you expect for the v1->v2 embed transition (they're planning a deploy June 15 and want to know if Redwood will be routing)?
- For customers that ask for an exception (pinned models), what's the criteria and approximate turnaround for an exempted rollout?

Maya
DataBridge Integrations
[Attachment: acme-dep-matrix-v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya@databridge.io>, Acme Platform <ops@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heads up: Acme using legacy /v1/embed endpoint (needs migration)

Thanks Maya — looping in Product and Ops.

Marissa / Priyom / Neha: can you review the attached matrix and confirm:
1) Planned deprecation window we intend to enforce for the v1 embed (target + hard cutoff).
2) Exception criteria: technical (pinned KV/weights), contract (paid add-on/legacy SLA), and duration limits.
3) Who owns customer comms and the proposed cadence (we typically send an initial notice, a follow-up reminder 2 weeks before, and a final cutover notice).

Acme: to set expectations, we want to give customers an explicit runway wherever possible. If you can flag the most business-critical teams on your side, we can prioritize an exception evaluation.

I'll coordinate a short triage call Friday if that helps.

- Karthik
Head of Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Maya R. <maya@databridge.io>, Acme Platform <ops@acme.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heads up: Acme using legacy /v1/embed endpoint (needs migration)

Adding Product detail and an initial recommendation.

Short answers:
- Target runway: we recommend a 60-day notice-to-cutover window. Target start: June 1, hard cutoff: July 31. Rationale: gives customers time to validate model outputs and update SDKs.
- Exception criteria (proposal):
  * Accepted: temporary pin for customers on active paid contracts with documented technical blockers (e.g., irreversible fine-tuning tied to old embedding hashes). Exceptions are timeboxed (max 90 days) and require an exception request form + Eng sign-off.
  * Rejected: general procrastination, untested internal apps without business impact justification.
- Owners:
  * Comms: Marissa (customer-facing notices) + Karthik (partner comms to DataBridge).
  * Exception intake & technical review: Prio/m (Priyom) + Neha for infra/ingress risk review.

Action items:
1) Priyom: intake template for exception requests (form + required evidence) by Mon 2027-05-24.
2) Neha: quick infra risk checklist (latency/regression risk and gating criteria) by Tue 2027-05-25.
3) Marissa: draft notice templates and timeline for Acme-specific cadence by Wed 2027-05-26.

I'll attach a proposed comm cadence (proposed-comm-windows.md) once ready.

-Marissa
Senior PM, API Platform

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Maya R. <maya@databridge.io>, Acme Platform <ops@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heads up: Acme using legacy /v1/embed endpoint (needs migration)

Thanks — attached is a rough intake checklist I'm proposing (see inline).

--- intake checklist (summary) ---
1) Customer name + primary contact (email/phone)
2) Exact endpoints & model hashes pinned
3) Business impact summary (who breaks, which downstream jobs)
4) Evidence: logs showing pinning, example payloads, failing test vectors
5) Requested exception duration + justification
6) Contract reference (if applicable)
7) Rollback/mitigation plan from customer (if they plan feature flags)

Notes: exceptions will get a 72-hour technical triage once submitted. If a customer matches criteria #1-4 above and has a valid business-critical justification, we move to a timeboxed temporary allowlist while Eng & Infra build required mitigations.

Maya / Acme: please use this checklist when submitting any formal request so we can fast-track triage.

- Prio/m
Principal Solutions Engineer
[Attachment: proposed-comm-windows.md (md)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Maya R. <maya@databridge.io>, Acme Platform <ops@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heads up: Acme using legacy /v1/embed endpoint (needs migration)

Triage update and infra constraints.

Summary of infra review:
- Routing: we can support a per-customer allowlist for the old endpoint for up to 90 days with feature-flag gating. It requires a small config change and an SRE runbook for monitoring (latency & error SLOs).
- Risk: customers with high request volume (>1M tokens/day) on legacy endpoints will need rate-limits or dedicated capacity to prevent tail latency impacts.
- Regressions: we require a lightweight smoke test suite (3-5 test vectors) from the customer to validate outputs across the v1->v2 model mapping.

Next steps:
1) Acme to submit formal exception intake using Priyom's checklist this week.
2) Marissa to share customer-facing notice draft; we'll align on the dates: proposed start June 1, final cutoff July 31.
3) Karthik and DataBridge: please confirm whether you want Redwood to auto-route traffic during the June start window (we can, but it requires a signed routing permission doc).

I'll stand by for the intake form. If Acme needs an emergency short extension, they should include the specific jobs and an ETA for remediation.

-Neha
Head of Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference
